sentences.text: Pseudocorax was a cartilaginous fish belonging to the class Chondrichthyes.
The genus was first described by Priem in 1897, with Pseudocorax affinis serving as the type species.
Scientists have recorded 81 distinct fossil occurrences of this ancient predator.
Its remains have been discovered across a vast range including Europe, the Middle East, North Africa, and North America.
The genus currently contains six valid species, such as Pseudocorax heteromorphus and Pseudocorax laevis.
Once placed in the family Anacoracidae, it is now classified in its own family, Pseudocoracidae, alongside Galeocorax.
Two species formerly assigned to this genus, Pseudocorax australis and Pseudocorax primulus, were later reidentified as Echinorhinus and Squalicorax.
This animal lived from the Aptian to the Bartonian, spanning between 119.57 and 37.71 million years ago.
